findings.title: A link can overwrite a visitor’s Pi answer
findings.description: `ask()` increments `newest`, but the load loop continues to the next `?q=` query after an interrupted browser run resolves. If a visitor clicks Ask the Pi while the first query in a multi-query link is loading, the next linked query replaces their SQL and can suppress or overwrite the Pi result.

findings.title: An unrequested waiting line appears
findings.description: `ask` writes a `Asking the Raspberry Pi.` paragraph into the result area before the request starts. The ticket's acceptance criteria say nothing about a waiting state, so the ticket does not ask for this line. It is a new visible behaviour on the page and it reaches the result area until the reply arrives.

findings.title: Unrequested explanatory paragraph added
findings.description: The `index.html` change adds a second paragraph of explanatory text under the buttons and rewrites the existing hint to begin with `Run:`. The ticket asks only for a second button next to the run button and for the result text, so this copy is an addition the ticket does not request.

findings.title: Pi requests set unrequested fetch options
findings.description: `askPi` passes `credentials: "omit"` and `cache: "no-store"` to `fetch`, in addition to the method, body and signal. The ticket asks for a `POST` with the query text and nothing about credentials or caching, so these options are new request behaviour that the ticket does not ask for.

findings.title: Run and Ask the Pi cancel each other
findings.description: `ask` increments the shared `newest` counter, so a click on `Ask the Pi` makes a pending browser `run` discard its result, and a click on `Run` makes a pending Pi answer disappear. The ticket asks for no such interaction between the two buttons, and it is a new cancellation rule added to the existing browser engine path.
